content.title: David Spade and Theo Von Release Self-Financed Comedy Bus Boys
content.text: Published Apr 18, 2026 - 05:13 Last Update Apr 18, 2026 - 05:13 © Bus boys movie hits theaters today, David Spade and Theo Von's comedy drops nationwide Smallest Font Largest Font Actors David Spade and Theo Von released their self-financed buddy comedy, Bus Boys, in theaters across the United States on Friday, April 17, 2026. Directed by Jonah Feingold, the film follows two friends who believe working in the service industry will resolve their personal struggles.The production, which has a runtime of 1 hour and 33 minutes, received an R-rating due to its language, drug content, and sexual themes. Spade and Von co-wrote and produced the feature, opting to bypass traditional Hollywood studio distribution to maintain creative control over the project. The plot centers on characters Markie Montgomery and Steefen ‘Steef’ Barn, residents of an Arizona border town. According to IMDb, the duo is convinced that securing jobs as waiters is the key to their redemption, though they must first prove themselves as busboys. "A pair of idiot friends believe that if they become waiters, all of their problems will be solved. They aren’t entirely wrong, but they aren’t entirely right" stated an official synopsis provided by the production. Filming for the project took place in Brockton, Massachusetts, providing a specific regional setting for the narrative. This follows earlier production work conducted in Los Angeles during the January 25 fires. The creators utilized a digital marketing firm to reach audiences directly, leveraging Von's existing podcast following.Movie Production DetailsDetailInformationRelease DateApril 17, 2026GenreComedyDirectorJonah FeingoldFormatNationwide theatrical releaseThe supporting cast features several notable comedians and performers. Tim Dillon appears as Manager Tim, Bobby Lee plays Samuel, and Jay Pharoah portrays a DEA agent. Other cast members include Leah McKendrick, Nate Diaz, Trevor Wallace, and Jimmy Gonzales, according to cast lists from Rotten Tomatoes and Wikipedia. Both lead actors invested their own capital into the venture to ensure the final product matched their specific comedic vision. Theo Von confirmed on his podcast that the self-financing model allowed the team to make every creative decision regarding the script and production style. 0 Like 0 Dislike 0 Funny 0 Angry 0 Sad 0 Wow
